A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EQ-VAE work and contain readable equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Although v3 removes the appendix contents entries, the corresponding appendix material remains available.

before.justification: v1 reports original autoencoder fine-tuning, reconstruction, equivariance, and ImageNet generation results, including ablations in Section 4.4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, including results for continuous and discrete autoencoders and downstream generative models.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same implicit equivariance objective, mixture with standard autoencoder training, spatial transformations, and application before quantization for discrete autoencoders.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenImages for fine-tuning and ImageNet for generation and reconstruction evaluation. The scaling and rotation scenarios are unchanged; no dataset, task, or domain coverage is added.

E2.justification: The main and appendix tables retain the same autoencoder and generative-model comparators. Newly cited Ryu (2024) appears only in related work, not as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The stated training budgets, batch sizes, model configurations, preprocessing, guidance settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same 50,000-image evaluation and equivariance transformation sets.

E4.justification: The transformation, fine-tuning-duration, additional-training, explicit-versus-implicit, and regularization-strength ablations retain their evidence. The intrinsic-dimension analysis and appendix qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SD-VAE rotation/scaling errors from 0.93/0.80 to 0.89/0.69 and its EQ-VAE counterpart from 0.49/0.15 to 0.56/0.43, reducing the reported equivariance advantage. Generation and reconstruction scores remain unchanged. Appendix Table 7 retains the earlier equivariance values.

T1.justification: The spatial-transformation and equivariance definitions, training-objective equations, and Appendix C.3 equivariance-error definition are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about equivariance regularization, compatibility with continuous and discrete autoencoders, preserved reconstruction quality, and accelerated generative training, including the sevenfold DiT speedup.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning latent-space complexity, complementary scaling and rotation effects, anisotropic scaling's reconstruction tradeoff, and explicit regularization's collapse behavior remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, autoencoder specifications, interpolation details, evaluation hardware, estimator implementation, and project/code access information are retained. The added repository reference documents prior work rather than new reproduction instructions for EQ-VAE.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Marcos et al. (2017) and Ryu (2024). It explicitly acknowledges Ryu's flip-equivariant autoencoder training while distinguishing its lack of investigation into latent generative modeling, providing a focused refinement of research positioning.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized related-work rewriting, affiliation edits, and replacement of the placeholder ICML running header with the paper title. The main exposition and section sequence remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix contents list disappears while its heading remains. Table 8 and Appendix B consequently move from page 13 to page 12, leaving page 13 sparse. Publication information is added on the first page; figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves acknowledgement of closely related work and corrects the running header. However, its revised Table 1 errors disagree with the retained Table 7 values for corresponding rows without explanation, and appendix navigation deteriorates. The PDFs do not establish whether the numerical revisions improve accuracy, so these benefits and reporting regressions do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
